title: Cache class design
idea: The cache class design splits storage from the eviction decision: `BoundedCache` stores entries, and an `EvictionPolicy` names which key to drop when it is full.

analogy.text: A small reading desk holds a few books. A rule card on the desk says which book goes back to the shelf when a new one arrives.
analogy.breaks: The rule card sees only key events, never the book contents.

points: `Cache<K,V>` is the interface callers use: get, put, remove, size.
`BoundedCache` owns the map and the capacity check, nothing about order.
`EvictionPolicy` hears every put, hit and removal, then names a victim.
An eviction listener lets callers react without the cache knowing them.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: Callers depend only on the interface, so any implementation can be swapped in.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: BoundedCache implements Cache and enforces the capacity.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: A HashMap gives O(1) average lookups. It knows nothing about recency.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: BoundedCache reports each event to its policy and asks it for a victim when full.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: LruPolicy keeps keys in use order and names the oldest as the victim.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: LfuPolicy plugs into the same slot later, without editing BoundedCache.

edges.label: notifies
edges.caption: After each eviction the cache calls the listener, for logs, metrics or cleanup.

code.title: Interfaces and core
code.caption: The whole design in one file: two interfaces, one policy, one bounded store, and a short demo.

walk.text: Build a two-entry cache with LRU and a listener that prints evictions.
Reading dish:1 makes it recent, so the next full put drops dish:2.
A zero capacity is refused when the cache is built.
The policy contract: three events in, one victim out.
LRU keeps keys oldest first; touching a key moves it to the end.
Only a hit is reported to the policy; a miss changes nothing.
A new key in a full cache evicts the victim first, then stores and records.

pitfalls: Do not put recency logic in the store; it blocks adding LFU later.
Refuse null values, or a stored null looks the same as a miss.
Replacing an existing key must not evict anything; check `containsKey` first.

quiz.q: What is the first line ClassDesign prints?
quiz.why: The get on dish:1 makes it most recent. When dish:3 arrives the cache is full, so LRU evicts dish:2 and the listener prints it.

takeaway: Store entries in one class; let a pluggable policy choose the victim.

starters: Why is EvictionPolicy generic only in K and not V?
Should the policy or the cache own the capacity?
How would I add a weight per entry instead of a count?
